tip: The sya ending on бреется (breyetsya = shaves) turns the action back on the doer, so he shaves himself with no separate object.
Here the sya ending means 'each other', not 'oneself': встречаемся (vstrechaemsya = we meet one another), so no extra word is needed.
по лестнице (po lestnitse = up the stairs) shows how po governs the dative for movement along a surface.
A past-tense verb plus the particle by makes the conditional 'would': Он бы помог (on by pomog = he would help), which is not about the past.
надеется на лучшее (nadeyetsya na luchsheye = hopes for the best): the verb takes na plus the accusative, not a bare object.
быть вежливым (byt vezhlivym = to be polite): a describing word after 'to be' goes in the instrumental, so not вежливый (vezhlivy).
приближается к финишу (priblizhaetsya k finishu = approaches the finish): the verb pairs with k plus the dative for what you near.
возвращаемся из отпуска (vozvrashchaemsya iz otpuska = returning from vacation): motion out of a place uses iz plus the genitive.

english: She is preparing for the exam.
tip: готовится к экзамену (gotovitsya k ekzamenu = prepares for the exam): the verb takes k plus the dative for what you prepare for.
Я бы мог приехать (ya by mog priyekhat = I could come): mog plus by softens a plain 'can' into 'could' or 'might'.
должен был позвонить (dolzhen byl pozvonit = should have called): dolzhen byl expresses past obligation, 'had to' or 'should have'.
свой (svoy = one's own) changes to match its noun: свой дом (svoy dom, m), своя машина (svoya mashina, f), своё место (svoyo mesto, n, here).

english: We would like to visit the museum.
tip: хотели бы посетить (khoteli by posetit = would like to visit): a want verb plus by becomes the polite 'would like', softer than a plain want.

english: Bring me a glass of water, please.
tip: стакан воды (stakan vody = a glass of water): a container word takes the genitive for its contents.

target: Мы добираемся до работы на метро.
english: We get to work by metro.
tip: на метро (na metro = by metro): na plus the prepositional names the means of transport, so not 'on the metro'.

target: От станции до дома десять минут.
english: It's ten minutes from the station to home.
tip: От станции до дома (ot stantsii do doma = from the station to home): the pair ot X do Y puts both places in the genitive.

target: Если бы я мог, я бы помог.
english: If I could, I would help.
tip: Если бы я мог, я бы помог (esli by ya mog, ya by pomog = if I could, I would help): hypothetical conditionals put by plus past in both halves.

target: Передай привет от меня своей маме и сестре.
english: Say hello from me to your mom and sister.
tip: Передай привет (peredai privet = say hello): the set phrase literally means 'pass a greeting' and is how you send regards to someone.

target: Не опаздывай на урок, учитель этого не любит.
english: Don't be late for the lesson, the teacher doesn't like that.
tip: Не опаздывай (ne opazdyvai = don't be late): negative commands use the imperfective verb, warning against the action in general.

english: He is amazed at the results.
tip: удивляется результатам (udivlyaetsya rezultatam = is amazed at the results): the verb takes the dative for what surprises you.

english: The house is being built quickly.
tip: Дом строится (dom stroitsya = the house is being built): with a non-living subject, the sya ending makes a passive, done by someone unnamed.

english: He is considered the best student.
tip: считается лучшим учеником (schitaetsya luchshim uchenikom = is considered the best student): the verb takes the instrumental for the label.

target: Пишите разборчиво, чтобы все могли прочитать.
english: Write legibly so that everyone can read it.
tip: чтобы все могли (chtoby vse mogli = so that everyone could): with different subjects in the two clauses, chtoby takes a past-tense verb.

target: Поставь будильник на семь утра, чтобы не проспать.
english: Set the alarm for seven in the morning so you don't oversleep.
tip: чтобы не проспать (chtoby ne prospat = so as not to oversleep): with one subject across both halves, chtoby takes the infinitive.

target: Переведи этот текст на русский язык к завтрашнему дню.
english: Translate this text into Russian by tomorrow.
tip: Переведи (perevedi = translate, informal) commands one friend; adding te, as in Переведите (perevedite), makes it formal or plural.
обижается (obizhaetsya = gets offended): the sya ending marks a change of state, like English 'get' plus an adjective.
справляемся с трудностями (spravlyaemsya s trudnostyami = cope with difficulties): this verb needs s plus the instrumental for what you handle.
A singular informal command takes the present-tense stem and adds -и (-i): переведёшь (perevedyosh) becomes Переведи (perevedi = translate).
A plural or polite command ends in -ите (-ite): Отдохните (otdokhnite = rest). Drop the -те (-te) for one close friend.
Давай plus a perfective we-form makes a let's suggestion: Давай встретимся (davay vstretimsya = let's meet).
